title: Record why a toolpath is stale: part stamps and values beside the combined stamp (#4245 step 2)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
## Summary

This is a step-2 item of the UI plan #4245: "Record why a toolpath is stale". The maintainer accepted the step-2 items as design issues (comment of 2026-11-27 08:09 on #4245). Code starts only when the maintainer accepts the design note below.

## What happens today

- An operation has three states: Never, Ok and Stale (`OpStatus`, `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).
- Generation stores one digest, `GenStamp(u64)`, in `Operation::stamp` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/generate.rs`). The project file keeps it as `stamp: Option<u64>` (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs`).
- `status_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`) compares the stored digest with the digest of the live world. A difference gives Stale.
- The digest is one `DefaultHasher` stream. Many inputs go into it: the version salt and the law tags, the tool (`stamp_tool::write`), the parameters with the resolved heights (`OpParams::stamp_with`, `params/digest.rs`), the geometry source, the stock and the setup (WCS origin and yaw, alignment, stated rotary axes), the area controls (`op_stamp`, `boundary_ctx.rs`) and the program ahead.
- `stale_reason` cannot read which input moved. It asks the world some live questions: is the tool there, is each source there, is each picked feature there, does each height resolve, did the program ahead change. When no question fires, it says "the geometry or tool inputs changed since it was generated".

The mockup E1 of #4245 shows a reason with a value: "stock top moved Z 0.000 → Z 1.000". The fallback text does not tell the user what to check.

## Design note (for acceptance)

### Rule 1: the combined stamp stays the only judge

`GenStamp` stays the only test for Ok against Stale. The post gate and `status_of` do not change. The new records explain a Stale state. They never make one. Thus a fault in the new code can give a wrong reason, but it cannot make a stale toolpath read as current.

The combined stamp keeps its bytes. No saved project reads Stale because of this change.

### Rule 2: part stamps, taken in the same pass

A new hasher type `StampHasher` replaces `&mut DefaultHasher` in the stamp functions. It feeds each write into two hashers:

- the combined hasher, which gives the same `GenStamp` as today;
- the hasher of the current part.

The code that writes a group of inputs sets the part first. The parts:

| Part | Inputs today | Reason text (example) |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | the salt, `GENERATOR_OUTPUT_VERSION`, the law tags (#2965, #3077, #4062 and others) | "CamCraft changed how this operation is made - generate it again" |
| `tool` | `stamp_tool::write`, the wire and sinker conditions | "the tool 'EM-0600-4FL' changed" |
| `params` | the parameter values in `stamp_with` | "a parameter of this operation changed" |
| `heights` | the resolved heights (`digest::wh`, `digest::wh_opt`) | "Top moved Z 0.000 → Z 1.000" |
| `geometry` | the source placement and `geometry_signature`, the picks, the sketch digest | "the model 'Part1' moved or changed" |
| `stock` | the stock source, the stock box | "the stock top moved Z 0.000 → Z 1.000" |
| `setup` | WCS origin and yaw, the part alignment, the stated rotary axes, the machine | "the setup 'Setup 1' changed (work offset)" |
| `area` | the area controls in `op_stamp` | "the area limits changed" |
| `prior` | the program ahead (rest machining) | today's `prior_stale` text |

There is one pass and the cost is two hashers. It needs no second walk over the world.

### Rule 3: a few values, for the words "from → to"

A hash tells that a part changed, but not the old value. Generation also records some small values:

- each resolved height (the name and the Z);
- the stock box (min and max);
- the work offset origin of the setup.

The live values come from the same functions. The reason then shows the old and the new value.

### Rule 4: the order of the questions

`stale_reason` keeps today's live questions first. They are exact: a deleted tool, a deleted source, a lost pick, a height that does not resolve. Then it compares the parts in the order of the table and names the first part that moved, with values where it has them. If more than one part moved, it names the first part and adds "and N more inputs".

If every part moved, the build changed (`DefaultHasher` is stable only inside one build, as the comment on `GenStamp` says). The reason then says "CamCraft was updated since this toolpath was made - generate it again". If the operation has no part record (an older project file), the reason stays today's general text.

### Rule 5: the project file

`OperationDto` gets one optional field, `stamp_parts`, next to `stamp`. It holds the part digests and the values of rule 3. `PROJECT_VERSION` goes up by one. The step-up is the version alone: an older file has no field and reads as `None`. A save without parts writes no key, so a project without them saves the same bytes.

### Rule 6: where the reason shows

- The operation page (`op_page.rs`) shows the reason now. It gets the new text without other changes.
- The Browser row and the issues pane of #4245 (PR I) use the same function.
- MCP: the operation list says "stale". It gets an optional `stale_reason` field with the same text. This is an addition, and no tool changes its arguments.

### What does not change

- No toolpath and no posted G-code changes.
- No `GenStamp` value changes. No operation goes Stale because of this change.
- The post gate stays as it is.

### Options dropped

- **Store a copy of all the inputs, and compare it field by field.** This gives the best text. But it doubles the parameter data in the project file, and each new parameter needs compare code. Dropped.
- **Make the combined stamp the hash of the parts.** This is simpler. But each saved project reads Stale one time after the update. Dropped: rule 1 keeps the old bytes.
- **Compute the parts only when the user asks for the reason.** The old parts are not available at that time. Dropped.

## Tests (when the note is accepted)

- A height edit gives "Top moved Z a → Z b".
- A moved stock gives the stock text with the old and the new value.
- A new tool diameter gives the tool text.
- A project file without `stamp_parts` gives today's general text. It saves and loads the same bytes.
- The `GenStamp` of each recorded test project stays the same (a golden of the stamp values).
- A change of the law tag gives the `version` text.
- Each test that exists for `stale_reason` (`crates/app/tests/operations.rs`, `stamp_tests.rs`) keeps its text.

## Effort and safety

`effort:high`. The work changes the stamp code and the project file. Rule 1 keeps the Ok and Stale result exactly as it is today, so the safety floor does not apply to the judgement. The review must check that `GenStamp` keeps its bytes.

Done means: the maintainer accepts the design note; then one PR does rules 1 to 6 with the tests above, and the operation page shows the new reason.

Parent: #4245.
